'''Dario Graffi''' (10 January 1905 – 28 December 1990) was an influential Italian [[mathematical physicist]], known for his researches on the [[electromagnetic field]], particularly for a mathematical explanation of the [[Luxemburg–Gorky effect|Luxemburg effect]],<ref name="Morro1993.p32">{{harv|Morro|1993|p=43}}.</ref> for proving an important uniqueness theorem for the solutions of a class of [[Fluid dynamics|fluid dynamics equations]] including the [[Navier-Stokes equation]],<ref>See for example {{harv|Serrin|1963|loc=§5}}, {{Harv|Morro|1993|p=42}}, {{Harv|Fabrizio|2012|p=184}}.</ref> for his researches in continuum mechanics and for his contribution to [[oscillation theory]].<ref>{{Harv|Fabrizio|2012|pp=184–185}}.</ref>

==Life and academic career==
Dario Graffi was born in Rovigo, the son of Michele, a [[yarn]] [[Wholesaling|wholesale trader]] and of Amalia Tedeschi.<ref name="GNFM.Fab">See reference {{harv|Consiglio Scientifico del G.N.F.M.|1999|p=XI}} or its English translation in {{harv|Fabrizio|2012|p=189}}.</ref> He attended the [[Secondary education in Italy#Istituto tecnico|Istituto tecnico]] in his home town, specializing in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]], but got his [[diploma]] in Bologna in 1921, where his family had moved a year before.<ref name="GNFM.Fab" />

He graduated from the University of Bologna in Physics in 1925,<ref name="RidCer">{{harv|Ridolfi|1976|p=357}}, {{harvs|last=Cercignani|year=1992|year2=1992a|loc1=p. 101|loc2=p. III}}</ref> when he was 20,<ref name="Morro1993.p42">{{harv|Morro|1993|p=42}}.</ref> and in mathematics in 1927,<ref name="RidCer" /> when he was 22:<ref name="Morro1993.p42" /> both the degrees were awarded [[cum laude]],<ref>{{harv|Ridolfi|1976|p=357}}, {{harvs|last=Cercignani|year=1992|year2=1992a|loc1=p. 101|loc2=p. III}}: {{harvtxt|Morro|1993|p=42}} seems to state only that he graduated ''cum laude'' in physics.</ref>

===Honors===
He was awarded the Golden medal "[[Benemeriti della Scuola, della Cultura, dell'Arte]]" in 1964, and a year later, the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] awarded him the [[Prize of the President of the Italian Republic]].<ref name="Premio.Lincei" />

==Work==

===Research activity===

Graffi is known for his researches on the [[electromagnetic field]], particularly for a mathematical explanation of the [[Luxemburg–Gorky effect|Luxemburg effect]], for proving an important uniqueness theorem for the solutions of a class of [[Fluid dynamics|fluid dynamics equations]] including the [[Navier-Stokes equation]],<ref>See for example {{harv|Serrin|1963|loc=§5}}.</ref> for his researches in continuum mechanics and for his contribution to [[oscillation theory]].

==Selected publications==
Graffi published 181 works.<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Cercignani|1992|p=104}}: {{harvtxt|Morro|1993|p=42}} states that Graffi published 181 scientific works.</ref> lists of his publications are included in references {{harv|Cercignani|1992|pp=108–114}} and in the [[#{{harvid|Consiglio Scientifico del G.N.F.M.|1999}}|biographical section of his "Selected works" (1999]], pp.&nbsp;XX–XXVI): however, the set of lecture notes {{harv|Graffi|1981}} is not listed in any of his publication lists.
